q: The rate of doing work is defined as ____.
e: Power measures how quickly work is done or energy is transferred.

q: The unit for power in SI units is the ____.
e: One watt equals one joule of work done per second.

q: If the work done is 1 joule in 1 second, the power is ____.
e: This defines the standard SI unit of power.

q: The units of power which are larger than watt are kilowatt (kW) and ____.
e: These are common units for expressing large amounts of power.

q: In the CGS system, the unit of power is ____.
e: This is the power unit in the centimeter-gram-second system.

q: In the British system, the unit of power is ____.
e: It expresses power as work done in foot-pounds per second.

q: In British engineering system, the unit of power is ____.
e: Horsepower is commonly used to rate engines and motors.

q: If the work done in 1 second is 550 ft-lb, the power is ____.
e: This defines the mechanical horsepower unit.
This conversion links SI and CGS power units.
This is the CGS equivalent of one horsepower.

q: For uniform motion, $P = Fv$ where $v$ is ____.
e: Power equals force times velocity when motion is uniform.

q: Power is not a fundamental concept like energy but it is a very important concept for ____.
e: Power is crucial in designing and rating machines and devices.

q: Car engines, water pumps, refrigerators, air conditioners and electric bulbs, etc., are specified according to their ____.
e: These devices are rated by how much power they use or deliver.
